prf:atom-knot-unique:
Proof Proof of atom knot unique. The Markov trace on B_n factors through the Hecke algebra: it is the composite of the quotient map B_n \to H_n(q), \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i, with the Ocneanu trace on H_n(q) (Jones–Markov trace). Two braids with the same image T_w in H_n(q) therefore have the same Markov trace, and the trace of a braid is the invariant of its closure. \square

Scope. The previous version of this proof concluded that the closures are isotopic, treating the Hecke quadratic relation \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1 as a Reidemeister II move. It is not one: Reidemeister II is \sigma_i \sigma_i^{-1} = 1, which holds already in B_n, while the quadratic relation identifies braids that are not isotopic. Uniqueness of the normal form (Diamond Lemma, hecke normal form) is a statement about H_n(q), not about B_n.
def:isotope-knot:
Definition Isotope as a knot variant of fixed proton block. Two atom-knots K_1, K_2 of types (Z, N_1) and (Z, N_2) with N_1 \neq N_2 are isotopes iff their NF block decompositions agree on the proton-quark block:

  T_{w_1} \;=\; T_{w_{q^Z}} \cdot T_{w_{\bar q^{N_1}}^{(1)}} \cdot T_{w_{\mathrm{inter}}^{(1)}},
  \qquad
  T_{w_2} \;=\; T_{w_{q^Z}} \cdot T_{w_{\bar q^{N_2}}^{(2)}} \cdot T_{w_{\mathrm{inter}}^{(2)}},

with identical w_{q^Z}.
rem:isotope-knot-properties:
Remark Isotopes are knot-distinct with independent stability. Two isotopes are knot-distinct. The Markov closures of T_{w_1} and T_{w_2} generally have different Jones polynomials whenever N_1 \neq N_2. The neutron-quark blocks contribute distinct Hecke generators. Isotopes are distinct knots, not the same knot at different aether parameters.

Stability per isotope is independent. The LP-dual ILP-feasibility is computed on the full NF T_w. This includes the w_{\bar q^N} and w_{\mathrm{inter}} blocks. Different isotopes can have different stabilities at the same q. This is the categorical analogue of the classical observation that {}^{12}\mathrm{C} is stable while {}^{14}\mathrm{C} is not.

Equivalence relation. The isotope relation is an equivalence on \{\text{atom-knots with fixed } Z\}. The relation is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive. The isotope class of K at fixed Z is parameterized by the neutron-quark block w_{\bar q^N} and the inter-nucleon connector w_{\mathrm{inter}}.
prop:isotope-knot-equivalence:
Proposition A reflexive, symmetric, transitive isotope relation is an equivalence. Let \sim be a relation on atom-knots with fixed Z, and assume that \sim is reflexive, symmetric and transitive. Then \sim is an equivalence relation.

Whether the isotope relation of def:isotope-knot satisfies these three properties is not part of this statement; they are hypotheses.
prf:isotope-knot-equivalence:
Proof Proof of isotope knot equivalence.

  • Reflexivity: K \sim K by definition since w_{q^Z}^{(1)} = w_{q^Z}^{(2)} = w_{q^Z} for K_1 = K_2.

  • Symmetry: K_1 \sim K_2 iff w_{q^Z}^{(1)} = w_{q^Z}^{(2)}, which is symmetric in K_1, K_2.

  • Transitivity: If w_{q^Z}^{(1)} = w_{q^Z}^{(2)} and w_{q^Z}^{(2)} = w_{q^Z}^{(3)}, then w_{q^Z}^{(1)} = w_{q^Z}^{(3)} by transitivity of equality in S_{n(K)}.

The equivalence classes at fixed Z are parameterized by the neutron-quark block w_{\bar q^N} and the inter-nucleon connector w_{\mathrm{inter}}. This gives the standard isotope chart for element Z (for example, Z = 6: {}^{12}\mathrm{C}, {}^{13}\mathrm{C}, {}^{14}\mathrm{C}, \ldots). \square

Quotient structure. The quotient \{\text{atom-knots}\}/{\sim} at fixed Z is the element class for Z. This recovers the chemical element concept categorically: an element is an isotope class.
conj:jsj-decomposition-linearity:
Conjecture JSJ additivity of nucleon braids. Let \mathcal{K}(Z, N) denote the atomic knot complement of an isotope with Z protons and N neutrons (atom knot). The inter-nucleon braids form essential tori, the complement decomposes under the Jaco--Shalen--Johannson (JSJ) decomposition into Z proton-block pieces and N neutron-block pieces with isotope-independent volume quanta \mathrm{Vol}_p and \mathrm{Vol}_n, and consequently

  \mathrm{Vol}\bigl(\mathcal{K}(Z, N)\bigr) \;=\; Z \cdot \mathrm{Vol}_p \;+\; N \cdot \mathrm{Vol}_n .

Additivity of hyperbolic volume over the pieces of the geometric decomposition along essential tori is a theorem of 3-manifold topology (Thurston). The conjectural content therefore lies entirely in the decomposition hypothesis: that the atomic knot complement JSJ-decomposes along the inter-nucleon tori into exactly Z proton and N neutron hyperbolic pieces, each carrying an isotope-independent volume quantum.

If the decomposition hypothesis holds, the linearity persists in the macroscopic topological limit: as the crossing number of a heavy-isotope knot grows large (crossing numbers well beyond 10^3), the total volume tracks the linear JSJ sum rather than exhibiting nonlinear growth. This scaling consequence would provide a structural backstop for extrapolating nucleon volumes to heavy isotopes; it is heuristic exactly to the extent that the decomposition hypothesis is open.
def:stable-atom:
Definition Stable atom (Frobenius positivity of the normal form). Let K be an atom-knot (atom) with normal form T_w \in H_{n(K)}(q). Let \mathrm{G}(q) be the Frobenius Gram matrix of the primitive Wedderburn-block operators \{e_\lambda\}_{\lambda \vdash k,\;k \leq k_{\max}}. Decompose the normal form in the primitive basis:

  T_w
  \;=\;
  \sum_\lambda x_\lambda \cdot e_\lambda,
  \qquad
  x_\lambda \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}.

The coefficient vector x(K, q) := (x_\lambda)_\lambda is determined by T_w. The atom K is stable at q if and only if this vector is an integer point of the positivity cone:

  x(K, q) \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^N
  \quad\text{and}\quad
  \mathrm{G}(q) \, x(K, q) \;\geq\; 0
  \;\text{coordinatewise.}
rem:stable-atom-properties:
Remark Properties of ILP stability. Independence of neighborhood. Stability is a fixed-q property. It does not require the ILP to be feasible on a neighborhood of q. An atom may be stable at q_0 and unstable at q_0 + \epsilon without contradiction. Stability tracks ILP-feasibility pointwise.

Connection to LP-feasibility. The continuous LP relaxation (x \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^N, \mathrm{G}(q) x \geq 0) is always feasible, since the trivial identity normal form T_e = e_{(k)} has y_{(k)} = 0. The ILP version is strictly stronger.

Confined operators only. One solves the ILP within the confinement filtration (confinement level) at q. One only considers primitives e_\lambda in J^{\ell(K, q)}(q), since operators above the atom's confinement level are unavailable without further phase transitions.

Scope of the stability condition. For a stable atom, the Frobenius positivity constraint (\mathrm{G}x)_\gamma \geq 0 holds for every primitive constraint \gamma at the coefficient vector of T_w itself. The condition is evaluated at the vector x(K, q) fixed by the decomposition of T_w, not at an arbitrary vector. The existential form \exists\, x \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^N with \mathrm{G}(q)\,x \geq 0 holds for every atom, since x = 0 satisfies it, and therefore does not distinguish stable from unstable atoms.
prop:stable-atom-decidable: Proposition Stability is decidable for any (Z, N) at fixed q. Let K be an atom-knot of type (Z, N) and let q be an aether parameter in the generic locus. Stability of the atom at fixed q is decidable. There exists an algorithm that returns True if K is stable at q and False otherwise.
prf:stable-atom-decidable:
Proof Proof of stable atom decidable.

  1. Compute the normal form T_w \in H_{n(K)}(q) via Gröbner–Shirshov reduction (hecke normal form). This terminates in finite time by the Diamond Lemma.
  2. Compute the confinement level (confinement level) \ell(K, q). Sort the finite set of shadow prices and find the smallest \ell such that T_w \in J^\ell(q).
  3. Construct the LP-dual constraint matrix \mathrm{G}(q) \in R^{N \times N}, where N is the number of primitive operators in J^{\ell(K, q)}(q). This set is finite by confinement-level-exists.
  4. Read off the coefficient vector x(K, q) of T_w in the primitive basis, check that it lies in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^N, and evaluate the N coordinates of \mathrm{G}(q)\,x(K, q). Over a ring with decidable order this is a finite computation.

Each step is decidable. Their composition is decidable. \square

Complexity. The bottleneck is step 1, the normal-form reduction. Step 4 is one matrix-vector product of size N. No integer-programming search is needed, because the vector being tested is fixed by T_w.
def:unstable-atom: Definition Unstable atom (failure of normal-form positivity). An atom-knot K is unstable at q if and only if it fails to satisfy the stable atom condition. That is, the coefficient vector x(K, q) of T_w within the confinement filtration J^{\ell(K, q)}(q) either fails to lie in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^N or violates \mathrm{G}(q)\,x(K, q) \geq 0 in some coordinate.
prose:intro-magic-shells: Unwrapping the integer-linear-programming solution counts across the (Z, N) plane isolates the nuclear magic numbers (2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126), the shell closures explained by the spin–orbit shell model of Goeppert Mayer [mayer1949] and of Haxel, Jensen and Suess, as points of Schur–Weyl self-duality where the active Wedderburn partition coincides with its conjugate (\lambda = \lambda'). This section proves the self-duality criterion, distinguishes the compound-\beta shell calibration from the single-wrap nuclear base, and defines the dimensionless magic-shell coupling \kappa.
rem:ilp-solution-count-unwrap:
Remark ILP solution count determines unwrap depth via confinement level. The number of distinct ILP solutions at a given confinement level dictates the unwrap depth required to uniquely specify an atom-knot's normal form.

Let K be an atom at aether parameter q with normal form currently expressed at level \ell. Let N_\ell(K, q) be the number of integer solutions x \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}^M to the Frobenius positivity ILP \mathrm{G}(q)\, x \geq 0 within the confinement filtration J^\ell(q).

The unwrap depth at level \ell is:

  d_\ell(K, q) = \max\bigl(0, N_\ell(K, q) - 1\bigr).

Interpretation:

  • N_\ell = 0: unstable at level \ell. The atom cannot exist in this shorthand. It must decay or fully unwrap.
  • N_\ell = 1: uniquely determined at level \ell. The shorthand suffices; no unwrap is needed.
  • N_\ell = k \geq 2: (k-1)-fold ambiguous at level \ell. One must unwrap k-1 levels to disambiguate via finer normal form structure.

Connection to confinement levels. Each unwrap step expands a shorthand word at level \ell into its normal form at level \ell - 1. The finer level accesses a larger filtration J^{\ell-1}(q) \supsetneq J^\ell(q). This richer operator basis distinguishes previously tied ILP solutions. When a coarse effective description exhibits multiple solutions, zooming to the next-finer scale resolves the ambiguity via operator content.

Computational benefit. Non-magic atoms typically exhibit N_\ell = 1 at the coarsest useful level. A single inter-nucleon configuration suffices. Magic atoms exhibit N_\ell \geq 2 at the nucleon level. Shell closure permits multiple equivalent assemblies of the closed shell. Each corresponds to a distinct normal form at the quark level. Double-magic atoms exhibit N_\ell \geq 3 because both proton and neutron closures contribute degeneracy.

Formal statement. Let K be an atom-knot. Then:

  \boxed{\; \text{NF-depth}(K, q) = \text{coarsest level } \ell \text{ with } N_\ell(K, q) = 1 \;}

Computing the normal form at exactly this depth fully specifies the atom's categorical structure. Deeper computation is redundant; shallower computation leaves ambiguity.

Example (proton gluon derivation). The proton's 9-crossing element \mathcal{B}_3 \times \Delta_3(\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}) admits N_\ell = 84 feasible ILP solutions at the baryon level. Minimizing |\mathrm{tr}_M| selects the unique \sigma_0 \to \sigma_0 solution. If a tie occurs, the framework demands unwrapping to the quark level, where the ILP separates them.

Computational shortcut. Adaptive unwrap reduces cost: storage and Gröbner reduction scale with n_{\text{strands}}^{\text{used}} rather than uniformly with 3A.
prop:shell-schur-weyl-self-duality:
Proposition Schur-Weyl justification of shell-operator self-duality. Let H_n(R, q) be the Iwahori–Hecke algebra with generators \sigma_i satisfying \sigma_i^2 = h\,\sigma_i + 1, where h = q - q^{-1}. The assignment

  \#\colon \sigma_i \;\longmapsto\; -\sigma_i^{-1} \;=\; h - \sigma_i

extends to an algebra automorphism of H_n(R, q). When H_n(R, q) is split semisimple, \# maps the central primitive idempotent e_\lambda to e_{\lambda^*}, where \lambda^* is the conjugate partition. Under quantum Schur–Weyl duality

  V^{\otimes n}
  \;=\;
  \bigoplus_{\lambda\,\vdash\,n}
    V_{\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{gl}_k)}(\lambda)
    \;\otimes\;
    V_{H_n(R, q)}(\lambda),

this is the Hecke-side form of the transpose \lambda \leftrightarrow \lambda^*.

Consequently, for

  \sigma_{\mathrm{shell}}
  \;=\;
  \sum_{\lambda\,\vdash\, A_{\mathrm{magic}}}
    x_\lambda \cdot e_\lambda
  \;\in\; H_{A_{\mathrm{magic}}}(q),

the shell-operator self-duality constraint

  x_\lambda \;=\; x_{\lambda^*}
  \qquad\text{for all}\quad \lambda \vdash A_{\mathrm{magic}}

holds if and only if \#(\sigma_{\mathrm{shell}}) = \sigma_{\mathrm{shell}}.

The transpose is not representation duality on the quantum-group side: in general V_{\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{gl}_k)}(\lambda^*) \not\cong V_{\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{gl}_k)}(\lambda)^*. For k = 2 and \lambda = (2) the two sides have dimensions 1 and 3.
prf:shell-schur-weyl-self-duality:
Proof Proof of shell schur weyl self duality. 1. \# is well defined. Put \tau_i = h - \sigma_i. From \sigma_i^2 = h\sigma_i + 1,

  \tau_i^2 \;=\; h^2 - 2h\sigma_i + \sigma_i^2 \;=\; h(h - \sigma_i) + 1 \;=\; h\,\tau_i + 1,

so \tau_i satisfies the Hecke quadratic. For adjacent i, j, expanding gives

  \tau_i\tau_j\tau_i - \tau_j\tau_i\tau_j
  \;=\; h^2(\sigma_j - \sigma_i) + h(\sigma_i^2 - \sigma_j^2) - (\sigma_i\sigma_j\sigma_i - \sigma_j\sigma_i\sigma_j),

which vanishes by the quadratic and braid relations. Far commutativity is immediate. Since \tau_i^2 = h\tau_i + 1 again, \# \circ \# = \mathrm{id}, so \# is an automorphism. The identity h - \sigma_i = -\sigma_i^{-1} follows from \sigma_i(\sigma_i - h) = 1.

2. \# transposes the blocks. In the split semisimple case, twisting the Specht module S^\lambda by \# gives the dual Specht module of \lambda^*, which is isomorphic to S^{\lambda^*} (see Mathas, Iwahori–Hecke algebras and Schur algebras, Ch. 3, and [dipper-james1986]). Hence \#(e_\lambda) = e_{\lambda^*}. At q = 1 this is the twist by the sign character, V_\lambda \otimes \mathrm{sgn} \cong V_{\lambda^*}.

3. Fixed points. Applying \#,

  \#(\sigma_{\mathrm{shell}}) \;=\; \sum_\lambda x_\lambda\, e_{\lambda^*} \;=\; \sum_\lambda x_{\lambda^*}\, e_\lambda .

The e_\lambda are linearly independent, so \#(\sigma_{\mathrm{shell}}) = \sigma_{\mathrm{shell}} if and only if x_\lambda = x_{\lambda^*} for every \lambda. \square

Scope. Steps 1 and 3 are proved here. Step 2 is cited.

Relation to existing propositions. Whether \sigma_{\mathrm{shell}} is in fact \#-invariant is not settled here.
rem:shell-schur-weyl-self-duality-interp:
Remark Physical interpretation: shell closures as charge-conjugate-invariant braids. Shell closures in nuclei correspond to charge-conjugate-invariant braid elements in H_{A_{\mathrm{magic}}}(q). This categorical structure enforces three physical constraints:

  • Parity conservation. The nuclear strong interaction conserves parity because shell closures respect charge conjugation.
  • Isospin doubling. Proton-neutron interchange symmetry emerges at closed shells via isospin SU(2) doubling.
  • CP conservation. Shell-level CP violation vanishes because parity-odd channels cancel between \lambda and \lambda^* contributions.

Parity-violating phenomena arise at level 3 (the inter-nucleon pair), where conjugate symmetry breaks via skein asymmetry. At level 4 (the shell) these constraints hold exactly when the shell operator is invariant under the transpose automorphism \#; that invariance is a hypothesis here, not a proved property of \sigma_{\mathrm{shell}}.
prop:compound-beta-shell-calibration:
Proposition Compound β-decay calibration across magic shells. Let E_0^{(2)} = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta be the free-neutron β-decay Q-value, the CAL-2 proxy, kept as a symbol. A β-decay (Z, N) \to (Z+1, N-1) preserves A, so the shell it can cross is a proton or neutron shell: let it cross a magic number, either Z < Z_{\mathrm{magic}} \le Z+1 or N-1 < N_{\mathrm{magic}} \le N, with magic numbers in \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\}. Assume the parent contains \sigma_{\mathrm{shell}} and the daughter contains a different shell operator or a cross-shell transition. Then the Q-value of the magic-crossing decay is:

  \mathfrak{Q}_\beta(\text{magic-crossing})
  \;=\;
  E_0^{(2)} \cdot
  \Bigl(
    \bigl|\mathrm{tr}_M^{\mathrm{parent}}\bigr|
    \;-\;
    \bigl|\mathrm{tr}_M^{\mathrm{daughter}}\bigr|
    \;-\;
    \bigl|\mathrm{tr}_M^{\mathrm{e^- + \bar\nu}}\bigr|
  \Bigr).

Equivalently, the shell-binding target y_{\mathrm{target}}(A_{\mathrm{magic}}) correlates to the cumulative β-decay chain reaching the magic anchor via the categorical trace. To formalize the full binding scale, one combines multiple β-decay Q-values along the isobar chain through the magic anchor.

Scope. The single magic-crossing Q-value identity above rests on the categorical trace. The compound-chain extension — combining Q-values along the isobar chain to isolate a shell-binding target — is exploratory: it subtracts model-predicted non-magic Q-values (a circular step) and carries an unresolved unit mismatch. It is therefore not a fit-free calibration and is not wired into any production shell-binding target.
rem:compound-beta-shell-calibration-key-:
Remark Magic-crossing Q-value measures the difference of shell operators. Non-magic vs magic \beta-decays (key distinction).

For magic-crossing decays, the \mathcal{Q}_q-value measures the strict difference in shell-operator contributions between parent and daughter, never the absolute shell magnitude itself. The parent intrinsically carries \sigma_{\mathrm{shell}}. The daughter realizes a distinct shell operator or a cross-shell transition.
rem:compound-beta-shell-calibration-inte:
Remark Magic-shell calibration corollaries and open implementation. Corollaries.

  1. The shell y_{\mathrm{target}} values are never independently calibrated. They follow strictly from \beta-decay \mathcal{Q}_q-values and level-3 shadow prices.
  2. The shell sector introduces no new calibration. One retains E_0 = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta as the pure H^2 input for the three-calibration discipline. Shell binding derives entirely from decay-chain \mathcal{Q}_q-values and level-3 shadow prices.
  3. Predictions for all magic-anchor binding energies are contingent on the empirical \beta-decay Q-value table (the per-isotope measured Q-values). Beyond the single CAL-2 anchor E_0 = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta, that table is experimental input — so these predictions are not parameter-free: the shell sector adds no new aether calibration, but it consumes the measured \beta-decay chain as data.

Numerically, E_0^{(2)} = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta \approx 0.782 MeV, the measured free-neutron value.

def:magic-shell-coupling-kappa:
Definition The expression \kappa_{\mathrm{closed}} = -E_0 \log(1/h) / [3]_q!. Let q be an aether parameter and m_e a mass scale. The expression \kappa_{\mathrm{closed}} is

  \kappa_{\mathrm{closed}}(q, m_e)
  \;=\; -\,\frac{E_0 \cdot \log(1/h)}{[2]_q \cdot [3]_q},
  \qquad
  E_0 = \frac{m_e}{q(q-1)}, \quad h = q - q^{-1},

where [n]_q = (q^n - q^{-n}) / (q - q^{-1}) is the balanced q-bracket.
rem:magic-shell-coupling-kappa-remark:
Remark Status and proved properties of \kappa_{\mathrm{closed}}. No physical quantity is claimed for the expression \kappa_{\mathrm{closed}}. At the aether parameter it evaluates to \kappa_{\mathrm{closed}} \approx -1.0704. It was formerly proposed as the per-excess slope of a magic-shell coupling; that identification is withdrawn, for the reason recorded below. The name is retained because the corpus refers to it, not because the identification stands.

Reason for the withdrawal.

The expression was matched, to 3.4 \times 10^{-4}, against a measured value of \approx -1.0708\;\text{MeV}. That value is the electrostatic energy of {}^{3}He's pp pair, attributed to the proton–neutron interface asymmetry.

The fit that produced it ran at two anchors and disagreed with itself:

anchor excess (n_{pp} - n_{nn}) slope
{}^{3}He (2,1) +1 -1.0707908\;\text{MeV}
{}^{3}H (1,2) -1 +0.2023095\;\text{MeV}

Opposite signs, a factor of 5.3 apart. The hypothesis under test was that a single coefficient holds across the anchors, and the producing computation recorded that it does not. The {}^{3}He arm became the published value; the {}^{3}H arm was not carried forward.

Those two nuclides differ in exactly one respect besides the sign of the excess: {}^{3}He contains a pp pair and {}^{3}H does not. Restoring that electrostatic energy removes the discord. Both residuals become negative — under every radius model tried, including the one derived from \bar\lambda_\pi and two independent alternatives — and under the derived radius they agree to 0.021\;\text{MeV}, essentially the {}^{4}He residual of 0.022\;\text{MeV} measured where the excess vanishes identically.

A term proportional to (n_{pp} - n_{nn}) must change sign between anchors of excess +1 and -1. What survives the correction does not: it is an excess-independent offset of order 0.2\;\text{MeV}, three to fifteen times smaller than the matched value. The excess coefficient is zero.

That single diagnosis accounts for the two independent negatives found before it. No term of this form and size appears in mirror-split binding data at A = 3, 15, 39, because the coefficient vanishes. And the original fit contradicted itself because it was describing an electrostatic energy with a categorical form, and only one of its two anchors has one.

Proved properties of the expression.

The following hold independently of any physical reading, and are unaffected by the withdrawal.

The bracket is the canonical balanced q-integer: [n]_q as written here coincides the library's balanced q-integer, unconditionally and including on the degenerate locus, so this definition introduces no competing q-integer convention.

The denominator is a q-factorial. [2]_q \cdot [3]_q = [3]_q!, hence

  [2]_q \cdot [3]_q \;=\; [3]_q! \;=\; \frac{q^3}{y_{(3)}(q)},

the inverse Markov weight of the trivial partition (3) \vdash 3. This is the reusable content of the block. The index 3 is the strand count of a single nucleon — the nucleon is the Borromean link, carried by the braid word (\sigma_1 \sigma_2^{-1})^3 \in B_3 — and the same normalization appears in the Borromean observable F_{\mathrm{Bor}} = |\mathrm{tr}_M(\beta_{\mathrm{Bor}})| / y_{(3)}(q).

The sign is forced. For q > 1, m_e > 0, and 0 < h < 1: E_0 > 0, \log(1/h) > 0, and [2]_q, [3]_q > 0, so \kappa_{\mathrm{closed}} < 0. This is a property of the expression and is asserted of nothing else.

A separate question, deliberately not attached here.

After the electrostatic correction, an excess-independent offset of order 0.2\;\text{MeV} remains at A = 3 that the same form does not exhibit at A = 4, where its residual is 0.022\;\text{MeV}. That is a real and unexplained baseline. It is not the quantity this block was about, and giving it this block's name would repeat the error the withdrawal corrects.

def:quantum-dilogarithm-disambiguation:
Definition Quantum dilogarithm disambiguation: \Phi_q (product form) vs -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-z) (Kashaev integration limit). Two distinct functions appear in the QOU mass formulae. One must not conflate them:

Name Symbol Closed form Behaviour near z = 1
Quantum dilogarithm product \Phi_q(z) \prod_{k=1}^{\infty} (1 - q^{-k}z)^{-1} Unbounded (\Phi_q(0.989) \approx 6.7 \cdot 10^5 at q_0)
Symmetric q-dilogarithm (Kashaev limit) \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z) \sum_{n \geq 1} \dfrac{z^n}{n \cdot [n]_q} Bounded; -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-z) \in [0.1, 0.82] for z \in (0,1) at q_0

The historical paper-level identity:

  \Phi_q(z) \;\stackrel{?}{=}\; \int_0^z \frac{\ln_q(1+t)}{t}\,dt
       \;\stackrel{?}{=}\; \prod_{k\geq 1}(1 - q^{-k}z)^{-1}

is false. The integral evaluates to the bounded quantity -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-z), not the unbounded \Phi_q(z). The two sides differ by six orders of magnitude at z = 0.989.

Discipline

The canonical form of the mass-endomorphism tower uses -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-|V|), never \Phi_q(|V|), for every per-generator amplitude.

The \Phi_q product form explains the \sim 10^5 \times amplification at |V| \to 1 that originally caused the -737 MeV pathology. The corrected canonical mass formula abandons it entirely.
rem:gluon-stabiliser-ledger:
Remark The gluon ledger: what step 4 enumerates, and why the trefoil loses. Step 4 of the derived atom says the integer LP dual "selects the minimum gluon", and the proton block says it "enumerates all feasible gluon combinations and selects the configuration minimizing |\mathrm{tr}_M|". Neither says what the enumeration ranges over. This remark says it. The answer dissolves the question it was written to settle: nothing is excluded, so no exclusion argument is owed.

The feasible set. The confinement-layer operator selection rule frames the candidate search. The stabiliser K ranges over non-trivial braid words up to a crossing cap; the constraint is positivity of the resulting state on the Temperley--Lieb quotient; the objective is minimum crossing number with |\mathrm{tr}_M(x\cdot K)| as tiebreak. The producer behind the nucleon numbers enumerates words over \{\sigma_0,\sigma_1,L_+,L_-\} of length at most three — 4 + 4^2 + 4^3 = 84 candidates, which is the count the unwrap-depth remark reports for the proton at baryon level. So the range is not "combinations of L_\pm". It is every braid word inside the cap, and the four-letter alphabet composes to all six normal-form basis words, e^- included.

The electron word is inside it. The natural worry is why the stabiliser may not be e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0: it is a basis word exactly as L_\pm are, and like them it has \mathrm{Vol} = 0, so nothing topological separates them. It is not excluded. As a three-letter braid word it sits in the enumeration — reached as \sigma_0\cdot L_-, or as L_+\cdot\sigma_0 — and it is admissible: applied to either bare nucleon it leaves the state Frobenius-positive. It loses, and it loses under either objective the corpus states. On |\mathrm{tr}_M| it is beaten by an order of magnitude or more for both nucleons. On crossing count it costs three, and both nucleons have admissible stabilisers costing one or two. That is a defeat in the minimisation, not a prohibition, and it is the only answer the construction supports.

Nor is double counting. The gluon does redistribute normal-form weight from \sigma_1 into the e^- channel, so e^- is the output of stabilisation. That is a consequence of the selection, not a constraint on the search: an e^- input would be a different, worse candidate, not a quantity counted twice.

Hyperbolic volume decides nothing here. Where a competing channel carries a hyperbolic constituent, volume settles the selection outright — the Borromean rings carry 8G and a torus link carries none. That is what happens one step earlier, at the antiquark disposal. That route is unavailable at step 4. All five non-identity basis words are torus-type with \mathrm{Vol} = 0, so volume separates none of them, and the whole selection falls to \mathrm{tr}_M and crossing count.

Crossing-count open question. Both nucleons carry two gluon crossings rather than a two-versus-four asymmetry. For the neutron braid \mathcal{B}_3(\mathfrak{u},\mathfrak{d},\mathfrak{d}), the eleven-crossing decomposition — six crossings from \mathcal{B}_3, three from the quark triad, and two from the gluon stabiliser — yields \mathrm{net}(\mathfrak{n}) = +0.7976 on the k-ladder (whereas thirteen crossings give 1.2359). The proton construction likewise applies a single L_- = \sigma_1\sigma_0 of two crossings. Because both nucleons share the same gluon-crossing count, the mass splitting \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{n}} - \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} (and hence \mathfrak{Q}_\beta) does not arise from a gluon-crossing difference.

A narrower discrepancy remains between the one-crossing and two-crossing stabiliser readings: under the minimum-crossing objective of confinement-layer operator selection, a single-crossing stabiliser (\sigma_1, crossing count 1) strictly dominates a two-crossing stabiliser (\sigma_0\sigma_0 or L_- = \sigma_1\sigma_0, crossing count 2), so the two counts cannot both arise from the same objective without an additional tie-breaking or parity constraint.

The feasible set itself is well defined and e^- is strictly suboptimal within it; determining which stabiliser the canonical objective selects remains open.
def:categorical-neutron:

Coulomb charge.

  Q(\mathfrak{n}) =

def:categorical-meson:
Definition Meson (categorical). A meson is a valence-2 hadron: a quark--antiquark pair bound by the Hopf link \mathcal{L}_H. One forms the meson from two independent quark--antiquark productions, pairing a quark from one with an antiquark from the other:

  \mathfrak{M}
  = 
  T_{01} \cdot \mathcal{L}_H \cdot T_{10}

where:

  • T_{01} = \sigma_0\sigma_1 = L_+ is the up-type crossing pair (knot notation); its closure in B_3 is the unknot.
  • T_{10} = \sigma_1\sigma_0 = L_- is the down-type crossing pair.
  • \mathcal{L}_H = \sigma_0\sigma_1 binds the two constituents.

The full braid word is (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^2 \cdot \sigma_1\sigma_0, containing 6 crossings on 3 strands.

Normal form (step-by-step Hecke reduction). One writes h = h_{\mathrm{A}} = q - q^{-1} and applies the Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 = h\sigma_i + \mathbf{1} and the braid relation \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 = \sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_1.

Step 1. For the bound pair T_{01} \cdot \mathcal{L}_H = (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^2 = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_1, one applies the braid relation to the rightmost three generators to yield \sigma_0 \cdot \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 = \sigma_0^2 \cdot L_-. The Hecke relation reduces this to:

  (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^2 = h \cdot e^- + L_-

Step 2. One multiplies by T_{10} = \sigma_1\sigma_0:

Factor Product Hecke reduction
L_- \cdot L_- \sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 braid + Hecke: h \cdot e^- + L_+
e^- \cdot L_- \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 \cdot \sigma_1\sigma_0 two braid + Hecke steps: h^2 e^- + hL_+ + hL_- + \sigma_1

Collecting terms yields the exact normal form:

  \mathfrak{M}_+ =
  \underbrace{h}_{\sigma_1}\sigma_1 + \underbrace{(h^2 + 1)}_{L_+}\sigma_0\sigma_1 + \underbrace{h^2}_{L_-}\sigma_1\sigma_0 + \underbrace{(h^3 + h)}_{e^-}\sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0

At the CODATA root q_0 \approx 1.1100 (h \approx 0.2091):

  \mathrm{NF}(\mathfrak{M}_+) \approx 0.209\,\sigma_1 + 1.044\,L_+ + 0.044\,L_- + 0.218\,e^-

yielding \mathrm{net}(\mathfrak{M}_+) \approx +1.515.

The mirror meson \mathfrak{M}_- = T_{10} \cdot \mathcal{L}_H \cdot T_{01} maintains identical net amplitude but exchanges \sigma_1 for \sigma_0:

  \mathrm{NF}(\mathfrak{M}_-) \approx 0.209\,\sigma_0 + 1.044\,L_+ + 0.044\,L_- + 0.218\,e^-

Both mesons carry identical L_\pm (L_+ + L_-) and e^- content, differing only in the single-generator excitation.

Particle content. The dominant L_+ term (coefficient \approx 1.044) establishes the binding. The e^- component (\approx 0.218) encodes the residual lepton channel. In contrast, the bare quark--antiquark pair (T_{01} \cdot T_{10}) yields \mathrm{net} = +1.418 and contains a neutrino \nu component in place of the Hopf links. The Hopf link binding actively replaces the neutrino channel and increases the net amplitude by \approx 0.097.

rem:meson-scale-independence-calibration:
Remark Calibration structure and the volume-zero geometric core of meson-scale independence.

Calibration structure

The three calibration inputs are independent physical measurements. Each is associated with a decay process:

Anchor Observable Jet order Measurement
CAL-1 m_\mathfrak{e} h^0 electron mass (Penning trap)
CAL-2 P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta} h^2 neutron \beta-sector bar-skew channel (\tau_n = \hbar / P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta})

The h^1 jet order is absent. The bar involution q \mapsto q^{-1} forces all Markov traces of writhe-zero braids to be even functions of h. The h^3 order enters through the flavor-split X = (q-1)^2(1-q^{-4})/3 = h^3/6 + \cdots, which is a skein difference (not a single-braid Markov trace).

Because \mathrm{Vol}(\mathrm{Hopf}) = 0, the volume-proportional geometric contribution to the meson scale vanishes identically, independently of (m_\mathfrak{e}, q_0). Proof Proof of meson scale independence. (Representation-theoretic and topological.)

The baryon mass formula uses \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) / \hbar_q^2 as the geometric normalization. \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) = 8G > 0 is the hyperbolic volume of the Borromean complement. The meson's binding topology is the Hopf link L_+. Its complement is T^2 \times I, a Seifert-fibred space rather than a hyperbolic one, so \mathrm{Vol}(\text{Hopf complement}) = 0. Without a non-zero hyperbolic volume, there is no geometric invariant to set the meson mass scale from (m_\mathfrak{e}, q_0).

The Hecke character ratios under additional crossings are derived: \chi^{(3)}(K)/\chi^{(3)}(\pi) = q^2, \chi^{(2,1)}(K)/\chi^{(2,1)}(\pi) = 1/(h^2+1), \chi^{(1^3)}(K)/\chi^{(1^3)}(\pi) = q^{-2}. These determine m_K/m_\pi (given m_\pi) but not m_\pi itself. \square
rem:pion-mass-hyperbolic-threshold:
Remark Why m_\pi is a calibration: the pion sits below the hyperbolic threshold. The scale-independence proof attributes the missing pion scale to the meson's binding topology: the Hopf link complement is T^2 \times I, Seifert-fibred rather than hyperbolic, so \mathrm{Vol} = 0 and there is no geometric invariant to set m_\pi from (m_\mathfrak{e}, q_0). That is correct, but it reads as a fact about one link. It is a fact about where the pion sits in a ladder, and stating it that way explains the calibration structure rather than merely reporting it.

The ladder. The fundamental knot operator basis assigns the same braid word to three particles at successive powers:

n (\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1})^n closure type \mathrm{Vol}
1 \sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1} unknot trivial 0
2 figure-eight 4_1 hyperbolic hyperbolic \approx 2.0299

A correction the table invites. The operator basis describes the \mathrm{Vol} = 0 entries as "the massless, force-carrying sector". That reading is already contradicted inside the same table: the electron sits there with \mathrm{Vol} = 0 and is the mass unit of the whole framework. prose:eightfold-intro:
Introduction.

The previous chapter established the knot-particle dictionary: each observable particle corresponds to a specific braid configuration in the Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_n(q), and the confinement hierarchy organises these configurations into shells. The question this chapter takes up is: why do these particles fall into the octets and decuplets of the Eightfold Way of Gell-Mann and Ne’eman?

The candidate answer lies in the representation theory of three-strand braiding --- but the chapter must open with a warning about the shape of that answer, because the obvious reading of it is wrong.

Two different A_2s. The braid group B_3 and its q-deformation H_3(q) have Coxeter type A_2: the Coxeter quotient of B_3 is W(A_2) \cong S_3, permuting the three strands. This is true, but it is true by construction --- the braid group on n strands has Coxeter type A_{n-1} by definition, so choosing n = 3 is what puts A_2 there. It is not a structural theorem about the aether, and nothing is derived from it.

The A_2 that the eightfold way needs is a different one: the Lie algebra \mathfrak{sl}_3 of flavour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}}, which in quantum Schur--Weyl duality [jimbo1986] (the baryon-multiplet section) is the partner acting on the fibre V, and which appears only when \dim V = N = 3. The two A_2s coincide in name --- and in this chapter's diagrams --- solely because n = 3 has been set and N = 3 is wanted. Setting n = 3 does not make N = 3.

This distinction is the chapter's central honesty constraint, and the reason that section records the N = 3 problem as the chapter's principal open problem rather than as a solved step: the single-fibre construction of the braiding chapter yields a quantum form of \mathrm{SU}(2), with \dim V = 2, and no choice of q raises it. Every flavour-\mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} statement below is therefore conditional on N = 3, and is marked as such.

The root-system section derives the A_2 root system from the Hecke relations of H_3(q) and identifies the hexagonal weight lattice. The flavour-representations section constructs the flavor triplet and antitriplet from unknot configurations and assigns the charge quantum numbers (isospin I_3, hypercharge Y). The meson-octet section derives the meson octet via the tensor decomposition \mathbf{3} \otimes \bar{\mathbf{3}} = \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{1}, realised through the \bowtie_K product. The baryon-multiplet section extends to baryons: \mathbf{3} \otimes \mathbf{3} \otimes \mathbf{3} = \mathbf{10} \oplus \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{1}, with the symmetric channel yielding the decuplet and the Borromean baryon (Definition) providing the structural realisation. The colour-algebra section derives the color \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{c}} gauge algebra from octonionic stabilisation. The q-deformation section develops the q-deformation of the hexagonal weight lattice and connects it to the hyperbolic geometry of knot complements. The dictionary section consolidates the complete knot--particle--force dictionary. The open-problems section records the open problems.

Epistemic tiers. Each statement below is marked with one of four tiers, used in the same sense as in the Standard-Model appendix: proved (with a complete proof); derived (obtained from framework structure without fitted parameters); standard (a theorem of the ambient mathematics --- Coxeter theory, Schur--Weyl duality, \mathrm{SU}(3) representation theory --- cited, not re-derived here, and carrying no QOU content on its own); conditional (a rigorous consequence of a named hypothesis, principally N = 3); and open (a precisely identified missing object).

What this chapter does not do. It does not derive flavour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}}. The eightfold-way classification is reproduced conditionally on N = 3, and N = 3 is not available: the framework supplies \dim V = 2. Most of the representation theory below is tier standard --- correct, and correctly applied, but true of any \mathrm{SU}(3) and not evidence for the framework. What the chapter contributes is the placement of the braid dictionary against that classification, one derived entry (I_3 on the nucleon doublet), and a sharpened statement of what is missing. The consolidated ledger is the open-problems section.
prop:a2-from-three-strands:
Proposition The A_2 root system from the Hecke algebra H_3(q). The Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_3(q) has Coxeter type A_2, and the associated weight lattice supplies the (I_3, Y) coordinates used throughout this chapter.

Scope. This is a statement about the A_2 of the Coxeter group W(A_2) \cong S_3 acting on the three strands, and it holds by construction: the braid group on n strands has Coxeter type A_{n-1}, so n = 3 puts A_2 here by definition. Nothing about the aether is derived from it. In particular this is not the A_2 = \mathfrak{sl}_3 of flavour \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}}, which is the Schur--Weyl partner acting on the fibre V and requires \dim V = 3. Items 1--3 below are the standard braid/Coxeter dictionary, recorded for reference; item 4 and the weight-lattice paragraph are what the chapter actually uses.

Concretely:

  1. The generators T_1, T_2 of H_3(q) satisfy the braid relation T_1 T_2 T_1 = T_2 T_1 T_2 and the quadratic Hecke relation (T_i - q)(T_i + q^{-1}) = 0. The braid relation is the defining relation of the Coxeter group W(A_2) \cong S_3.

  2. The Cartan matrix of A_2 is

  a_{ij}
  = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 \end{pmatrix}.

This is read off from the Coxeter presentation in the usual way: the braid relation T_1 T_2 T_1 = T_2 T_1 T_2 has length m_{12} = 3, and a_{ij} = -2\cos(\pi/m_{ij}) gives a_{12} = a_{21} = -1, with a_{ii} = 2 by normalisation. For |i - j| > 1 the generators commute (m_{ij} = 2) and a_{ij} = 0. A counting formula of the shape a_{ij} = 2\delta_{ij} - |\{T_iT_jT_i = T_jT_iT_j\}| would only re-encode the presentation; it is not an independent derivation of the Cartan data.

  1. The six roots of A_2 are the elements \{\pm\alpha_1, \pm\alpha_2, \pm(\alpha_1 + \alpha_2)\}, where \alpha_1, \alpha_2 are the simple roots associated to T_1, T_2. The angle between adjacent roots is \pi/3 (that is, 120° between a root and its negative), reflecting the Coxeter number h = 3 of A_2. The Weyl group W(A_2) \cong S_3 acts by permuting the three strands.

  2. At q = 1 (the classical limit), H_3(q) reduces to the group algebra \mathbb{C}[S_3], and the A_2 root system is the standard one. For q \neq 1 (the aether-deformed case), the root system acquires a q-deformed inner product: the quantum Killing form \langle \alpha_i, \alpha_j \rangle_q = [a_{ij}]_q, where [n]_q = (q^n - q^{-n})/(q - q^{-1}) is the q-integer.

The hexagonal weight lattice of A_2 is the 2-dimensional lattice generated by the fundamental weights \omega_1, \omega_2 dual to the simple roots. Each irreducible representation of H_3(q) is labelled by a dominant integral weight (\lambda_1, \lambda_2) with \lambda_i \geq 0, and the weights of the representation sit at the vertices of a hexagonal pattern in the (I_3, Y) plane, where

  I_3 = \tfrac{1}{2}(\lambda_1 - \lambda_2),
  \qquad
  Y   = \tfrac{1}{3}(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2).

The fundamental representation \mathbf{3} has weights \{(1,0), (0,1), (-1,-1)\}, forming an equilateral triangle. The adjoint representation \mathbf{8} has weights forming a regular hexagon with multiplicity 2 at the origin.
rem:q-deformation-weight-lattice:
Remark The q-deformation and the invariance of the root datum. Two distinct occurrences of the integer 2 appear in the classical A_2 Serre relation and root system: one is a binomial coefficient that deforms into the Gaussian integer [2]_q = q + q^{-1} under Drinfeld–Jimbo quantization, whereas the other is the diagonal Cartan entry a_{ii} = 2 that remains constant for all q. Separating these two roles clarifies what the aether parameter q_0 deforms in the eightfold-way classification and what remains rigid.

The two 2s. The classical Serre relation for A_2 reads

  e_i^2 e_j - 2\, e_i e_j e_i + e_j e_i^2 = 0,

where the coefficient 2 is the binomial coefficient \binom{2}{1} = \binom{1 - a_{ij}}{1}, with a_{ij} = -1 the off-diagonal Cartan entry. Meanwhile, the diagonal Cartan entry is a_{ii} = 2, which appears in the root angle formula \cos\theta = a_{ij}/a_{ii} = -1/2, giving \theta = 120°.

The Drinfeld--Jimbo quantization replaces the binomial 2 by the Gaussian binomial [2]_q = q + q^{-1}:

  e_i^2 e_j - [2]_q\, e_i e_j e_i + e_j e_i^2 = 0.

The Cartan entry a_{ii} = 2 is untouched. The angle \cos\theta = -1/2 does not become \cos\theta_q = -(q + q^{-1})/2. These are two different mathematical objects that coincide numerically at q = 1: one is a binomial coefficient, the other is a normalization constant.

What is q-independent — proved here. The following are proved:

  • The off-diagonal entry a_{12} = -1 and the Serre exponent 1 - a_{12} = 2.
  • The q-Serre coefficient [2]_q genuinely moves with q --- witnessed at q = 2, where the framed binomial is 5 and the framed Cartan diagonal is 4 --- while the Cartan datum does not. The conjunction of the two is the "two 2s" separation , and it is the conjunction, not either half alone, that carries the content: constancy of the Cartan datum is true by construction and is compatible with both sides being constant, which is exactly the confusion at issue.
  • For (q-1)^2 \neq 0 the two differ ; they agree at q = 1 .
  • The root-angle ratio \cos\theta = a_{ij}/a_{ii} = -1/2 .

What is not established here. That Drinfeld--Jimbo quantisation leaves the root datum invariant is a theorem of Lusztig/Kashiwara, cited here and not proved in this work; it belongs to the "standard, but not proved here" list below, not to the proved list above. What is proved is the arithmetic of the separation on the A_2 datum, which is a weaker statement and should not be cited for the stronger one.

What is q-independent — standard, but not proved here. These follow from the Drinfeld--Jimbo construction and are cited here, not proved:

  • The root lattice \Lambda_R = \mathbb{Z}\alpha_1 \oplus \mathbb{Z}\alpha_2 and the weight lattice \Lambda_W = \mathbb{Z}\omega_1 \oplus \mathbb{Z}\omega_2.
  • The Weyl group W(A_2) \cong S_3.
  • Weight multiplicities: for generic q the representation category \mathrm{Rep}\,\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{g}) is tensor-equivalent to \mathrm{Rep}\,\mathfrak{g}. Crystal bases exist precisely because the weight combinatorics is q-independent (the q \to 0 limit retains the same lattice).

What q does deform.

  • The braiding: the R-matrix of \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3) depends on q and governs the braid group action on tensor products.
  • The quantum dimensions: \dim_q(V_\lambda) = \prod_{\alpha > 0} [\langle \lambda + \rho, \alpha^\vee \rangle]_q / [\langle \rho, \alpha^\vee \rangle]_q.
  • The Markov trace: \tau_q(\beta) on H_n(q) varies with q, producing q-dependent link invariants (Jones polynomial, HOMFLY-PT).
  • The crossing energy: \mathfrak{E}_\times(q) = \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}), which governs mass splittings in the framework.

Consequence for the eightfold way. The hexagonal weight lattice of A_2 is rigid under q-deformation. The octet and decuplet patterns do not "bend" or become hyperbolic at q = q_0. What changes is the dynamics on the lattice: transition amplitudes, mass splittings, and mixing angles all depend on q_0 through the Hecke algebra representations, while the classification pattern itself --- which states go where on the hexagon --- is q-independent.

The classification thus holds for any q, while the quantitative predictions (mass ratios, decay rates) are specific to q = q_0.
rem:flavor-charge-assignments:
Remark Flavor charge assignments and the hypercharge gap. The A_2 weight lattice of the A_2 proposition assigns two quantum numbers to each state: the third component of isospin I_3 and the hypercharge Y, related to the fundamental weights by

  I_3 = \tfrac{1}{2}(\lambda_1 - \lambda_2),
  \qquad
  Y   = \tfrac{1}{3}(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2).

The electric charge is then the Gell-Mann--Nishijima relation Q = I_3 + Y/2.

Derived quantity: isospin I_3. The writhe-to-isospin map w \mapsto I_3 is derived in the framework without fitted parameters. Over the nucleon doublet, the proton braid \mathfrak{p} and neutron braid \mathfrak{n} carry writhes whose difference reproduces \Delta I_3 = 1 scale-free. This identifies I_3 as the writhe coordinate on the A_2 weight lattice. These writhes are those of the inter-nucleon arc, w(\mathfrak{p}) = +1 and w(\mathfrak{n}) = -1. The ruled nucleon word (\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}^{-1})^3 is the same for both nucleons and has writhe 0, so on the word itself the writhe does not separate them; there I_3 is the weight of the up and down strand labels.

Open quantity: hypercharge Y. The proton and neutron share Y = +1 while their writhes differ. This falsifies every injective map from the writhe to Y, in particular the linear map Y = c\,w that a framing phase q^{w c} would give. It does not falsify every function of the writhe: a non-injective one such as Y = w^2/4 passes the proton–neutron test. What does force a second invariant is the charge side. The quark charges are not a function of the writhe (the anti-up and down crossings share the writhe -1 but carry -\tfrac{2}{3} and -\tfrac{1}{3}; see the Coulomb-charge definition), and if both Q and I_3 were functions of the writhe then so would be Y = 2(Q - I_3). Since I_3 is read here as the writhe coordinate, a hypercharge independent of the writhe requires a charge Q that is not the halved writhe. The framework therefore requires a second invariant, independent of the writhe, to instantiate Y.

The candidate direction, recorded without endorsement, is the ribbon-framing twist. In the categorical braid representation, each strand carries a framing datum whose total T(t) is independent of the crossing word (hence independent of the writhe w). The candidate hypercharge is

  Y_t = 2\bigl(Q_{\mathrm{twist}} - I_3\bigr),
  \qquad
  Q_{\mathrm{twist}} = \frac{T(t)}{3},

where T(t)/3 is the colour-tube charge quantum of the quark picture (the helon-model normalisation of Sundance O. Bilson-Thompson [bilson-thompson2005]; in the braided-ribbon-graph formulation of Sundance O. Bilson-Thompson, Fotini Markopoulou, and Lee Smolin [bilsonthompson2007, §I, §V], strand twists define noiseless U(1)-charged subsystems conserved under local evolution moves, without claiming to derive the Standard Model interactions). The Gell-Mann--Nishijima relation holds by construction if and only if Q_{\mathrm{twist}} = Q against an independently derived electric charge Q --- a falsifiable consistency condition. The halved writhe of the Coulomb-charge definition cannot play that role, since it is not the electric charge, so the condition has no derived right-hand side yet.

Status and batteries. Neither the candidate nor any alternative has been wired. Any hypercharge proposal must pass two batteries before instantiating the class:

  1. Gell-Mann--Nishijima consistency: Q = I_3 + Y/2 must hold against an independently derived Q and I_3 on the nucleon doublet, without tuning a coupling. No derived Q exists yet, so this battery cannot currently be run against anything but the Standard-Model table.
  2. First-generation spectrum: The Y values of u, d, e^-, \nu_e must reproduce \{+1/3, +1/3, -1, -1\} (left-handed) and \{+4/3, -2/3, -2, 0\} (right-handed), satisfying the \mathbb{Z}_6 compatibility relations of John C. Baez and John Huerta [baez-huerta2010].

A candidate requiring a fitted scale to pass either battery is a fit, not a derivation, and does not instantiate this class.

Enumeration result, and why it carries no corroboration. The battery has been run over all 10{,}000 helon-style assignments (3 strands per fermion, per-strand twist in \{-1, 0, +1\}), of which 4 survive. That ratio must not be read as a 2500\!:\!1 filter: the battery collapses to a single linear equation per flavour, and the surviving count is multiset counting. The following are proved:

  1. The spectrum battery is exactly T = 3Q. Both the candidate Y_t = 2(Q_{\mathrm{twist}} - I_3) and the target Y = 2(Q - I_3) carry the same -2I_3, which cancels. What remains is Q_{\mathrm{twist}} = Q --- the defining equation of Q_{\mathrm{twist}}, not a test of it. The battery constrains nothing about isospin.
  2. The nucleon-doublet check is entailed, by charge additivity alone: T_{\mathfrak{p}} = 2T_u + T_d = 3(2Q_u + Q_d) follows from T = 3Q on the quarks, so no surviving assignment can fail it. As implemented it also states one condition twice --- its second clause 2(T_{\mathfrak{p}}/3 - 1/2) = 1 clears to T_{\mathfrak{p}} = 3, which is its own first clause.
  3. The \mathbb{Z}_6 condition is not a filter. As implemented it is a function of the Standard-Model table alone and never sees the candidate assignment; it runs as an input assertion and cannot exclude any multiset.

So each flavour is filtered independently by one equation, and 4 = 1 \times 2 \times 2 \times 1 counts the multisets of three twists from \{-1,0,+1\} with the required totals 3Q = (2, -1, 0, -3). The u-quark twist \{0,1,1\} and the electron twist \{-1,-1,-1\} are the two totals admitting a single multiset --- a fact about writing 2 and -3 as a sum of three elements of \{-1,0,+1\}, not about the framework; the d-quark and neutrino each admit two. Passing the battery is therefore equivalent to choosing t with \sum_i t_i = 3Q, which is always possible.

The open content is unchanged and is the whole question: whether the twist multisets are forced by the framework's braid words rather than only consistent with them.

A derived-twist repair, tested and refuted (scope-(a)). The defect above is that t is a free label. The natural repair is to replace it with the canonical twist of the ribbon category --- on a simple object the twist acts by a scalar whose exponent is the content sum c(\lambda) = \sum_{(i,j) \in \lambda} (j - i), a derived per-block integer. Taking Q = c(\lambda)/3 is parameter-free. It does not work: at n = 3 the content sums are \{3, 0, -3\}, giving the integer charges \{+1, 0, -1\} with no third-integer charge at all, and no n \le 8 yields both quark charges \{+2/3, -1/3\} . This is scope-(a) for the plain content-sum reading, not an exclusion of the ribbon route: other normalisations remain untested.

What the hypercharge must supply for a Coulomb term. On the nucleon doublet lepton number vanishes, so the Gell-Mann--Nishijima hypercharge equals the baryon number, Y = B = 1 for both proton and neutron. Per strand this is B = \tfrac{1}{3}, and the strand charge Q = T_3 + B/2 gives u \mapsto \tfrac{2}{3}, d \mapsto -\tfrac{1}{3} and a three-strand block with a up strands the charge a - 1. So on the baryon sector the content of Y is a derived reading of B; the non-strange identification Y = B with the Milnor triple linking number of the three colour tubes is a conjecture with no instance, and the lepton sector further needs a lepton number for Y = B - L.

Hypercharge alone does not give a Coulomb pair term. The exchange of the unbroken neutral bosons between two particles has charge factor g^2\,T_3T_3' + g'^2\,(Y/2)(Y'/2), with no T_3 \otimes Y cross term. On two three-quark blocks (Y = 1, T_3 = \pm\tfrac{1}{2}) it takes the same value on the proton pair and the neutron pair: it is an isospin coupling with no Coulomb part. It splits identically as

  g^2\,T_3T_3' + g'^2\,\tfrac{Y}{2}\tfrac{Y'}{2}
  = e^2\,QQ' + g_Z^2\,(T_3 - s^2 Q)(T_3' - s^2 Q'),

with e^2 = g^2g'^2/(g^2+g'^2), s^2 = g'^2/(g^2+g'^2) and g_Z^2 = g^2+g'^2. The first term is the Coulomb factor, zero whenever a neutron is involved. On nucleon blocks the exchange with a fraction \lambda of the second term kept has the Coulomb form if and only if \lambda = 0, and the remaining coefficient e^2 vanishes exactly when g'^2 = 0. Coulomb is therefore the unbroken W^3 + B exchange minus the Z exchange, and it needs, besides Y: the mixing s^2 = \sin^2\theta_W, and a Z mass scale that removes the second term at nuclear distance. Neither is derived in this framework: the electroweak torus-link triplet of the electroweak conjecture orders m_W < m_Z < m_H by crossing number but fixes no absolute scale.

Split-bundle framing F = V_2 \oplus W_3^* and conditional hypercharge coupling. In the Standard Model appendix, the missing hypercharge and the missing three-dimensional partner are shown to be one conditional gap rather than two independent knobs. If the two-dimensional fibre V_2 (z_2 = q^3/(q^2+1)) is paired with a three-dimensional partner W_3^* (z_3 = q^3/[3]_q = q^5/(q^4+q^2+1), separated from z_2 by the identity z_2 - z_3 = q^3 / ((q^2+1)(q^4+q^2+1)) \neq 0) inside F = V_2 \oplus W_3^*, then over any field of characteristic outside \{2, 3\} the traceless centralizer \mathrm{diag}(y_2, y_2, y_3, y_3, y_3) satisfies 2 y_2 + 3 y_3 = 0 if and only if y_3 = -\tfrac{2}{3} y_2. Fixing the doublet normalisation y_2 = 1 pins y_3 = -\tfrac{2}{3}, gives the exterior-pair quark doublet in V_2 \otimes W_3^* hypercharge y_2 + y_3 = +\tfrac{1}{3}, and yields the Killing traces \mathrm{tr}(T_3^2) = \tfrac{1}{2} and \mathrm{tr}((Y_F/2)^2) = \tfrac{5}{6}, hence the unrenormalized Weinberg ratio \mathrm{tr}(T_3^2)/(\mathrm{tr}(T_3^2) + \mathrm{tr}((Y_F/2)^2)) = \tfrac{3}{8}. On single strands, combining the weak-crossing sign s_2 \in \{\pm 1\} with the W_3 versus W_3^* triality orientation \tau_3 \in \{\pm 1\} via Q = \tfrac{1}{2} s_2 + \tfrac{1}{6} \tau_3 reproduces (+\tfrac{2}{3}, -\tfrac{1}{3}, +\tfrac{1}{3}, -\tfrac{2}{3}) on (u, d, \bar d, \bar u) and separates \bar u (-\tfrac{2}{3}) from d (-\tfrac{1}{3}) by +\tfrac{1}{3} \neq 0 despite their identical crossing sign -1. This implication is proved conditionally on W_3^*: constructing W_3 categorically in the multi-fibre groupoid remains the open antecedent.
prop:meson-octet-decomposition:
Proposition The meson octet via \mathbf{3} \otimes \bar{\mathbf{3}}. The tensor product of the fundamental triplet and its conjugate decomposes as \mathbf{3} \otimes \bar{\mathbf{3}} = \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{1}, yielding the meson octet and the flavor singlet.

A meson is a quark--antiquark bound state. In the flavor \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} classification, a quark transforms in the fundamental \mathbf{3} and an antiquark in the conjugate \bar{\mathbf{3}}. The tensor product decomposes into the adjoint (octet) and the trivial (singlet) representations:

  \mathbf{3} \otimes \bar{\mathbf{3}}
  = \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{1}.
  \qquad (9 = 8 + 1)

The \mathbf{8} (adjoint representation) has weights forming a regular hexagon with double multiplicity at the origin, sitting in the (I_3, Y) plane. Weights are recorded in the quark-count coordinates (\lambda_1, \lambda_2) = (n_u - n_s,\; n_d - n_s) used for the \mathbf{3} in the A_2 proposition, so that the charge formulas I_3 = \tfrac{1}{2}(\lambda_1 - \lambda_2) and Y = \tfrac{1}{3}(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2) of that proposition apply verbatim to every row below:

Weight I_3 Y Meson identification
(1, -1) +1 0 \pi^+\ (u\bar{d})
(-1, 1) -1 0 \pi^-\ (d\bar{u})
(2, 1) +\tfrac{1}{2} +1 K^+\ (u\bar{s})
(1, 2) -\tfrac{1}{2} +1 K^0\ (d\bar{s})
(-2, -1) -\tfrac{1}{2} -1 K^-\ (s\bar{u})
(-1, -2) +\tfrac{1}{2} -1 \bar{K}^0\ (s\bar{d})
(0, 0)_a 0 0 \pi^0\ (u\bar{u} - d\bar{d})/\sqrt{2}
(0, 0)_b 0 0 \eta\ (u\bar{u} + d\bar{d} - 2s\bar{s})/\sqrt{6}

The \mathbf{1} (singlet) is the \eta':

  \eta' = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(u\bar{u} + d\bar{d} + s\bar{s}).

QOU realization. In the knot-particle dictionary, each meson is a quark--antiquark pair joined by the \bowtie_K product. The splitting \mathbf{3} \otimes \bar{\mathbf{3}} = \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{1} is the trace splitting of a rigid category. Let V be the fundamental of U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3) at generic q and V^* its dual, with coevaluation c\colon \mathbf{1} \to V \otimes V^* and evaluation e\colon V \otimes V^* \to \mathbf{1} (using the pivotal structure). The composite e \circ c is multiplication by the quantum dimension d = [3]_q = q^2 + 1 + q^{-2}, which is nonzero for real q \neq 0. Then p = d^{-1}\, c \circ e is an idempotent on V \otimes V^*. Its image is the singlet, the image of c, and the complementary idempotent 1 - p projects onto the kernel of e, the octet. At q = 1 this is the splitting of a 3 \times 3 matrix into its trace part and its traceless part. The Hecke algebra H_3(q) does not enter here: it has no three-dimensional irreducible and no tensor product of modules, and it acts on V^{\otimes 3} by Schur--Weyl duality, which is the baryon side.

The idempotent algebra holds in any k-linear category: given c\colon U \to W and e\colon W \to U with e \circ c = d \cdot 1_U and d \neq 0, the maps p and 1 - p are complementary idempotents, p \circ c = c, e \circ p = e, and e \circ (1 - p) = 0. The octet is not proved irreducible here, and U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3) is not constructed.

Conditional on N = 3. This decomposition requires the flavor fundamental to be three-dimensional (N = 3). The N = 3 question is the chapter's central open problem. The tensor decomposition itself is a theorem of \mathrm{SU}(3) representation theory; its applicability to QOU depends on resolving how the three-dimensional flavor space arises from the multi-fibre groupoid or octonionic stabilization.
rem:meson-mass-splitting:
Remark Meson mass splitting from q-deformed dynamics. The q-deformation lifts the mass degeneracy of the meson octet. The eight states share the same hexagonal weight pattern but their masses split through the quantum dimension and crossing-energy formulas of the Hecke algebra.

The meson octet decomposition (\mathbf{3} \otimes \bar{\mathbf{3}} = \mathbf{8} \oplus \mathbf{1}) determines which states exist. The mass splitting of these states is a separate, q-dependent phenomenon governed by the Markov trace and the crossing energy.

q-independent structure. The weight lattice and the state assignments (which meson sits at which (I_3, Y)) are q-independent (Remark). The hexagonal pattern itself --- \pi^\pm at (\pm 1, 0), K^\pm at (\pm 1/2, \pm 1), \pi^0 and \eta at the origin --- is determined entirely by the Cartan matrix A_2, which the Hecke relation encodes independently of q.

q-dependent dynamics. Within the hexagonal pattern, the physical masses are governed by three q-dependent ingredients:

  1. Quantum dimensions: \dim_q(V_\lambda) = \prod_{\alpha > 0} [\langle \lambda + \rho, \alpha^\vee \rangle]_q / [\langle \rho, \alpha^\vee \rangle]_q. At q = 1 these reduce to the classical dimensions (all integer); at q \neq 1 they split.
  2. Crossing energy: \mathfrak{E}_\times(q) = \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}), the energy cost per crossing in the Hecke algebra. This governs the mass contribution from each braid crossing in the meson's knot representative.
  3. Markov trace weights: \tau_q(\beta) assigns a q-dependent amplitude to each braid \beta, producing the mass endomorphism via the Frobenius integral.

The Gell-Mann--Okubo mass formula. In standard \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} flavour physics, the meson masses obey the Gell-Mann--Okubo relation

  4 m_K^2 = 3 m_\eta^2 + m_\pi^2.

Gell-Mann--Okubo cannot test this. The relation is not something the framework should derive, and its \approx 6\% experimental deviation is not comparable with the \approx 3.3\% figure from the q-deformation of the adjoint quantum dimension.

First-order \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} breaking means the mass operator is a singlet plus an octet piece transforming like \lambda_8, so that

  m^2(I, Y) \;=\; a \;+\; b\,Y \;+\; c\left(I(I+1) - \tfrac{Y^2}{4}\right)

for some constants a, b, c. Evaluated on the pseudoscalar octet --- \pi at (I,Y) = (1,0), K at (\tfrac12, \pm 1), \eta at (0,0) --- the Gell-Mann--Okubo combination collapses identically:

  4m_K^2 - 3m_\eta^2 - m_\pi^2 \;=\; 0
  \qquad\text{for \emph{all} } a, b, c .

This is proved over any commutative ring, together with the sharper consequence that two arbitrarily different breaking patterns give the same value of the combination, namely zero. In particular b --- the entire hypercharge dependence, which is the whole content of a breaking mechanism --- cancels .

Two consequences. First, if the QOU crossing-energy splitting is first-order octet then it reproduces Gell-Mann--Okubo automatically and exactly, and doing so is not evidence for the framework: every first-order octet model reproduces it equally well [gellmann1962, okubo1962]. Second, the only testable content is the \approx 6.4\% deviation, which measures the failure of first-order breaking through second-order operators and \eta--\eta' singlet mixing.

Second-order quantum Casimir curvature versus singlet mixing. An unconstrained second-order polynomial in (I(I+1), Y) surjects onto every scalar residual over \mathbb{Q}, so a second-order fit carries no separating power unless the operator is fixed in advance. Replacing the classical isospin Casimir by the parameter-free rational quantum Casimir d_q(I, Y) = [I]_q[I+1]_q - [Y/2]_q^2 [kleinkreisler1996] (which evaluates over any field without square roots to d_q(1,0) = q + q^{-1}, d_q(0,0) = 0, and d_q(\tfrac{1}{2}, \pm 1) = (q + q^{-1})/(q + 2 + q^{-1})) yields an (a, b, c)-independent ratio for M(I, Y) = a + b\,Y + c\,d_q(I, Y) (c \neq 0):

  \frac{4 M_K - 3 M_\eta - M_\pi}{M_\pi - M_\eta}
  \;=\;
  -\left(\frac{q - 1}{q + 1}\right)^{\!2}
  \;=\;
  -\frac{(q - q^{-1})^2}{([2]_q + 2)^2}.

At q_0, this bar-even ratio equals -2.7168 \times 10^{-3}. Because m_\pi^2 - m_\eta^2 < 0 on the pseudoscalar octet whereas m_\Sigma - m_\Lambda > 0 on the baryon octet, the same negative factor predicts the observed sign on both octets simultaneously (4m_K^2 - 3m_\eta^2 - m_\pi^2 > 0 and 2(m_N + m_\Xi) - 3m_\Lambda - m_\Sigma < 0). In magnitude, however, single-q_0 isospin curvature accounts for only 1.21\% of the observed 6.43\% isospin-averaged meson deviation (normalized ratio -0.2247) and 0.82\% of the -0.57\% baryon deviation (normalized ratio -0.3330), confirming that \eta--\eta' singlet mixing and higher-order \mathrm{SU}(3)_{\mathrm{f}} breaking dominate the empirical residual.

The \approx 3.3\% figure is not a competing prediction. It is the q-deformation of \dim_q of the adjoint, a dimension rather than a mass splitting, and not a quantity that can appear on either side of the relation. Comparing the two numbers was a category error, and the comparison is withdrawn.

Ordered 3-strand gluon clasp for neutral flavours. Two-strand torus closures T(2, n) have vanishing hyperbolic volume and cannot distinguish an ordered constituent pair (n_1, n_2) from its swap (n_2, n_1) under symmetric content maps. Mapping the ordered antiquark--quark generation pair (n_1, n_2) \in \{3, 5, 7\}^2 to the parameter-free 3-strand gluon-clasp braid \beta_{\mathrm{clasp}}(n_1, n_2) = \sigma_1^{n_1}\sigma_2^{-n_2}\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1} \in B_3 gives \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}) monodromy determinant 1 and trace 2 n_1 n_2 + n_1 + n_2 + 3 \in \{27, 41, 55, 63, 85, 115\} > 2 (strictly pseudo-Anosov across all nine generation pairs, while the real-aether S^{(2,1)} trace at q_0 stays inside (-0.760, -0.291) near its q = 1 value -1). Although the 2 \times 2 S^{(2,1)} trace is symmetric under n_1 \leftrightarrow n_2, both the rank-2 (z_2) and rank-3 (z_3) full H_3(q) Markov traces separate \bar D^0 \mapsto (5, 3) from K^0 \mapsto (3, 5) by exact closed-form multiples of q^2 - q^{-2} (+0.2125 at z_2 and +0.1442 at z_3 for q = q_0).

Conditional on N = 3 and on Y. Mass splittings between isospin multiplets (for example \pi against K) depend on the hypercharge Y, which is open (the flavour-representations section). Within an isospin multiplet (for example K^+ against K^0), the splitting is purely electromagnetic and arises from the writhe difference, which is derived.
